architecture_decisions: - AC-01 Immutable typed authority contracts: The new tool-authority subsystem exposes frozen typed contracts for capability grants, action policies, requests, approvals, decision, result, and audit contracts.
work_items: - Establish a small, typed, server-owned tool-authority boundary that can later let Parallax use explicitly authorized external capabilities for one application Project without exposing provider secrets to model-visible state, allowing user/model text to grant itself authority, or turning connector access into arbitrary shell, HTTP, deployment, or database execution.
validations: - The subsystem proves project/action scoping and negative authority behavior through a deterministic in-memory registry that proves project/action scoping and negative authority behavior.

AC-02: validate protected requirement — Every capability is bound to exactly one non-empty opaque project reference, and authorization rejects a request whose project reference differs from the registered capability even when capability ID, tool, and action would otherwise match.

AC-03: validate protected requirement — Authorization succeeds only by resolving an already-registered enabled capability. Unknown capability IDs, disabled grants, or request-supplied lookalike authority are denied; request content cannot create or widen registry authority.

AC-04: validate protected requirement — Authorization requires exact tool identity and an exact action policy from the registered capability. Tool mismatch and unknown action requests are denied rather than falling back to a broader permission.

AC-05: validate protected requirement — Each action has an explicit consequence classification. Destructive actions require approval by invariant, and every approval-required action is denied unless immutable approval evidence matches the exact request ID, capability ID, project reference, tool, and action.

AC-06: validate protected requirement — Capability construction rejects generic shell, command, subprocess, raw HTTP/network, or equivalent reserved tool/action identities, and the authority request contract contains no command, URL, headers, body, environment, or generic payload field.

AC-07: validate protected requirement — Capability, request, decision, result, and audit contracts expose only bounded identifiers, policy state, normalized result codes, and digests. They contain no provider credential fields, raw payload/error fields, hidden-reasoning fields, or arbitrary metadata map capable of persisting secrets.

AC-08: validate protected requirement — Audit construction distinguishes DENIED, SUCCEEDED, and FAILED outcomes. A denied authority decision cannot produce an execution-success record, and a provider/tool failure cannot be converted into a successful audit outcome.

AC-09: validate protected requirement — Equivalent registry state and equivalent authority input produce the same normalized decision and canonical request/result digests independent of Python object identity or unordered collection iteration.

AC-10: validate protected requirement — The first slice imports no provider SDK, executes no provider call, opens no network/shell escape hatch, adds no API route or database migration, and makes no change to shared authentication, Code/autonomy, or deployment paths.

AC-11: validate protected requirement — Focused tests prove denial for cross-project use, unknown capability/action, tool mismatch, disabled capability, missing/mismatched approval, generic shell/HTTP escape attempts, and any attempt to treat request data as a self-granted capability.

AC-12: validate protected requirement — The subsystem treats `project_ref` as an opaque caller-supplied authoritative binding and documents that serialized integration must adapt it to workstream #43's accepted Project identity without introducing a competing persistent project model.
risks: - The implementation may introduce a risk of exposing project secrets to model-visible state, which could lead to unauthorized access if not properly secured.
